fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.6.8.2 Impact of Shared Memory (Table6, ablated on SelfStarter): ALL shared-memory-removal variants exhibit the SAME failure pattern -- apparent execution SUCCESS with semantically INCOMPLETE outputs (misleading pass/fail signal). Without Shared Memory entirely: paper context reduced two orders of magnitude, yields a trivial script that succeeds only by checking for an output directory. Without Architecture Memory: runnable scaffold but core modules unimplemented. Without Structured Paper Memory: parser relies on mocked behavior, hollow summaries despite consuming 1.1M tokens. Without Interface Memory: later modules drift from earlier interface commitments, causing a failed configuration-parsing case to be treated as success. Explicit conclusion: 'token efficiency alone is misleading in long-horizon agentic reproduction; the memory layer is essential for enforcing semantic completeness and cross-stage consistency under context constraints.' benchmarks: ScreenshotVQA (novel benchmark introduced in this paper: 5,000-20,000 screenshots per sequence x 3 PhD students, 87 questions total) + LOCOMO
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.3.2: without explicit retrieval triggering, 'the language model often defaults to its parametric knowledge, which may be outdated or incorrect' -- worked example: user tells the agent 'The CEO of Twitter is Linda Yaccarino' (stored in memory), and days later when asked 'Who is the CEO of Twitter?' with that message no longer in the visible conversation history, the model may incorrectly answer 'Elon Musk' from stale parametric knowledge instead of consulting stored memory. Mitigated by the Active Retrieval mechanism: the agent is required to generate a topic BEFORE answering/acting, and this topic auto-triggers retrieval from all six memory components (top-10 per component), injected into the system prompt tagged by source -- eliminating the need for explicit 'search your memory' prompting on every turn.
cita: Wang and Chen (2025). MIRIX: Multi-Agent Memory System for LLM-Based Agents.
notes: Sec.1/Fig.1/Sec.3.1: six explicit memory components map almost 1:1 onto the RQ1 vocabulary -- Core Memory(persona+human blocks, always-visible)=TRABAJO; Episodic Memory(time-stamped events: event_type,summary,details,actor,timestamp)=EPISODICA; Semantic Memory(concepts/entities/relationships independent of time, w/ source field)=SEMANTICA; Procedural Memory(how-to guides/workflows/scripts as steps lists)=PROCEDIMENTAL; Resource Memory(docs/images/voice_transcripts)+screenshot-based multimodal input=MULTIMODAL; Knowledge Vault(verbatim secrets, folded into SEMANTICA facts here since no dedicated vault token exists). representacion=HIBRIDA: structured typed entries (fields per component) + multiple retrieval methods (embedding_match, bm25_match, string_match, Sec.3.2) -> retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING;GREP-ARCHIVOS. operaciones: WRITE(Memory Managers 'update their respective memories in parallel'), ADMISION(Meta Memory Manager 'determines which memory components are relevant, routing the input'), CONSOLIDACION('ensuring that redundant information is avoided within each memory type'), ACTUALIZACION(Core Memory 'triggers a controlled rewrite process' at 90% capacity; Semantic entries 'persist unless conceptually overwritten'). trigger: memory update fires 'when new input is received from the user' (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); app-level batching 'once 20 unique screenshots are collected, the memory update process is triggered' (PRESUPUESTO, count threshold). F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO): added WRITE, FIDELIDAD, COSTO, PROCEDIMENTAL. handoff=CONTENIDO: retrieved memory content (tagged by source component) is injected into the Chat Agent's system prompt. plan_estado=NO: Procedural Memory stores general how-to knowledge (workflows/guides), not active task/progress-state tracking.

fallos_mitigaciones: Central motivating problem (Sec.1): memory-less coding agents suffer 'silos and amnesia' -- crucial information is (i) eventually dropped from the current session's context, (ii) not shared between sessions, and (iii) not shared between agents working with different users -- 'each interaction starts a new learning loop which has a limited lifespan.' Mitigated by Spark's shared collective memory layer where every agent interaction is captured as a portable trace, merged into a collective knowledge space via continuous autonomous curation, and redistributed to agents facing similar future challenges -- restoring the self-healing property that human developer communities of practice had before AI intermediation. The curation loop also explicitly tracks 'which memory patterns and paths effectively guide (and do NOT guide) coding agents toward increasingly more optimal solutions', i.e. it learns from unsuccessful recommendation patterns, not only successful ones.
cita: Tablan et al. (2025). Smarter Together: Creating Agentic Communities of Practice through Shared Experiential Learning.
notes: Sec.1.1/3: Spark treats 'every coding agent interaction as a potential learning event' captured as a structured/portable 'trace' of experience -> mem_tipos=EPISODICA; traces are 'analyzed to extract generalizable knowledge patterns... clustered by semantic similarity, and curated' into best-practice recommendations -> mem_tipos also SEMANTICA(distilled patterns)+PROCEDIMENTAL(coding best-practice/API-usage guidance, the domain is explicitly software development). Sec.3.1 Knowledge Base: documentation 'represented in multiple modalities (such as embeddings or raw text search indices)'; Retrieval Agent uses a 'hybrid search-and-generation approach combin[ing] generic semantic similarity estimates via vector search, text search at multiple levels of lexical scope' -> representacion=HIBRIDA, retrieval=EMBEDDINGS;RANKING. operaciones: WRITE('Spark captures multi-level contexts around each coding problem, the recommendation...and feedback'), ADMISION(curation 'in relation to different optimization criteria' gates what becomes durable curated knowledge vs raw trace), CONSOLIDACION('extract generalizable knowledge patterns, clustered by semantic similarity, and curated'), ACTUALIZACION('Memory-augmented Learning: Memory is augmented based on feedback'; 'Retrieval rankings are refined based on what worked...previously'). trigger: trace capture 'after each interaction' (EVENTO-DETERMINISTA); curation runs over 'Memory Epochs' that 'repeat iteratively' (CHECKPOINT, Sec.3.2). Sec.'Paper Summary'+Sec.4.4: separately measures (a) downstream code-quality lift from WITH-SPARK vs NO-SPARK across 3 models on DS-1000, AND (b) 'the intrinsic quality of recommendations generated by Spark against a wide range of criteria... helpfulness levels of up to 98.2%' -- a direct intrinsic evaluation of retrieved/generated recommendation quality -> mide_lectura=SI, F RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. alcance=ORGANIZACION: explicitly a 'shared agentic memory... used collectively by a group of AI agents operating in the same broad task domain' across DIFFERENT users/agents (community-of-practice scope), broader than a single project. multiagente=SI (the paper's core premise: multiple coding agents jointly contribute to and draw from one memory). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: recommendation workflow explicitly includes step 6 'referencing and linking specific sections' of source documentation, and curation tracks 'what worked (and did not work) previously' as evidence for knowledge quality. Fig.1: WITH-SPARK lifts mean code quality (1-5 LLM-judge scale) above NO-SPARK for all 3 models (Qwen3-Coder-30B, Haiku-4.5, GPT5-Codex), with a small open-weights 30B model matching a much larger frontier model's quality when boosted -> metricas=EXITO. F differs from F_screening(WRITE;MULTIAGENTE): added CONSOLIDACION, RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO, FIDELIDAD. handoff=CONTENIDO: recommendations (documentation excerpts, API examples, curated best-practice pointers) are the substantive content redistributed from the collective memory to individual agents. plan_estado=NO.

benchmarks: custom simulated 4-agent MAS environment (500 epochs); voting accuracy evaluated against a custom human-annotated set of 200 memory items; no public benchmark (future work explicitly proposes AgentBench)
fallos_mitigaciones: Central topic: 'ensuring that distributed memories remain synchronized, relevant, and free from the accumulation of outdated or inconsequential data -- a process analogous to biological forgetting' in multi-agent settings, while guarding the collective forgetting DECISION itself against Byzantine (malicious or faulty) agents. Mitigated by three integrated mechanisms: (1) multi-scale temporal decay (short/medium/long-horizon exponential decay combined into a threshold-gated staleness score, triggering forget PROPOSALS, not automatic deletion) to flag stale items; (2) DistilBERT-based context-aware semantic relevance re-scoring (beyond pure time-based heuristics); (3) PBFT consensus tolerating up to f Byzantine agents among N>=3f+1, requiring 2f+1 matching votes across pre-prepare/prepare/commit phases before any memory item is actually deleted -- reported 92% consensus success rate under simulated Byzantine fault injection, with the remaining 8% failing safely (item re-evaluated next epoch) rather than corrupting the memory state.
cita: Duong (2025). PBFT-Backed Semantic Voting for Multi-Agent Memory Pruning.
notes: QUALITY/RECONSIDERAR FLAG (integrity concern beyond ordinary low-rigor): the Results section (Sec.V) contains verbatim editorial/meta-commentary that appears to be unedited LLM-generated analysis leaked into the published text, e.g. 'The user's original draft mentioned a 16% improvement; this 88% accuracy represents a substantial level of correctness. (If the 16% was an improvement *over a baseline*, that baseline would need to be defined and tested against)' and 'Further analysis would involve...ablation studies removing the semantic component...However, the current evaluation provides strong evidence for the protocol's viability.' This strongly suggests the reported numbers/discussion were drafted by an LLM assistant without careful human review before submission -- a serious signal for human reconsideration of inclusion/reliability of the reported statistics, even though the architecture description (Sec.III, Algorithms 1-4) is coherent and internally consistent; extracted per protocol, decision left to human reviewer. Sec.III-A: 'These memories are centrally indexed and stored...but the decision to retain or forget a memory item is a collective one' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(generic shared knowledge base, content type unspecified beyond 'knowledge-based systems'); representacion=HIBRIDA(Pinecone 768-dim vector embeddings + SQLite structured metadata/UUIDs). operaciones=OLVIDO(the protocol's entire purpose: 'Co-Forgetting Protocol' for 'synchronized memory pruning')+ACTUALIZACION('Commit Changes: All deletions are then committed...ensuring memory state is consistently updated'); no WRITE/ADMISION contribution claimed (paper addresses pruning of ALREADY-stored items, not initial admission). trigger=CHECKPOINT('an epoch is triggered every 100 agent interactions', Sec.III-D) + EVENTO-DETERMINISTA(within each epoch, decay score D(t)<delta deterministically triggers a forget PROPOSAL, Algorithm2). retrieval=EMBEDDINGS(Pinecone vector similarity infrastructure + DistilBERT semantic relevance scoring). mide_lectura=NO: no evaluation of retrieval/read quality for downstream task use -- only forgetting-DECISION accuracy (vs human annotation) and cache-hit-rate (an access-latency efficiency metric, not a quality-of-content-read metric). alcance=PROYECTO: shared knowledge base persists for the MAS's whole operational lifetime (500 simulated epochs), not task-bound. multiagente=SI (4-agent weighted PBFT voting, 2 planning-weighted + 2 perception/execution-weighted). fidelidad_procedencia=NO: no source/staleness-of-CONTENT verification described (agent reliability confidence ci weights VOTES, not provenance of memory content itself). benchmarks: GSM8K, AIME24, AIME25, GPQA-Diamond, MedQA, ARC-Easy, ARC-Challenge, MBPP-Plus, HumanEval-Plus
fallos_mitigaciones: Sec.3.1 'Input-Output Distribution Alignment': directly inserting freshly generated last-layer hidden states H as input embeddings for the next latent step risks OUT-OF-DISTRIBUTION activations, because these dense high-level representations 'differ from the statistical patterns of learned token embeddings' -- an unmitigated naive design would degrade downstream generation quality. Mitigated (training-free) by a linear alignment operator W_a (computed once via pseudo-inverse of the output embedding matrix, W_a ~= W_out^+ W_in, and reused across all subsequent latent steps) that maps each output hidden vector back into the valid input-embedding space, keeping the alignment cost computationally negligible while preserving distributional consistency between latent and discrete representations.
cita: Zou et al. (2026). Latent Collaboration in Multi-Agent Systems.
notes: Abstract/Sec.1/3.2: 'a shared latent working memory preserves and transfers each agent's internal representations and latent thoughts' -- explicitly named 'working memory' -> mem_tipos=TRABAJO (scoped to a single multi-agent reasoning run over one question, not persisted across tasks/sessions). Sec.2 'KV Cache as Working Memory': memory = layer-wise Key-Value caches (accumulated dense hidden-state vectors), not a retrieval-oriented vector DB -> representacion=VECTOR (continuous vector representations; PARAMETROS rejected since this is runtime ACTIVATION state, not the model's trained weights). Sec.3.1-3.2: each agent auto-regressively APPENDS new last-layer hidden states to its own KV cache (WRITE); cross-agent transfer PREPENDS the predecessor's full layer-wise KV cache into the successor's (ACTUALIZACION/extension of working memory) -- no filtering, forgetting, or admission gate: transfer is explicitly WHOLESALE and 'lossless' (Theorem3.3), not selective -> retrieval=NA (nothing is selectively retrieved; the ENTIRE prior working memory is always transferred in full), mide_lectura=NO (no measurement of selective-read precision; the paper instead formally PROVES full-transfer fidelity, captured under fidelidad_procedencia). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: transfer happens at a fixed architectural point (after an agent completes its m latent steps, deterministic pipeline sequencing across Sequential/Hierarchical MAS), not LLM-discretionary. fidelidad_procedencia=SI: 'Communication Fidelity' is one of the paper's three foundational principles, formalized in Theorem3.3 ('Information Preservation via Latent Working Memory') proving outputs are equivalent to directly inputting the preceding agent's full output -- an explicit, proven content-fidelity guarantee. alcance=TAREA: latent working memory transferred within ONE inference run over a single question, not persisted. multiagente=SI (sequential planner/critic/refiner/solver and hierarchical code/math/science+summarizer settings, 5 backbone models). Table1-3: up to 14.6% higher accuracy vs baselines -> metricas EXITO; 70.8%-83.7% output-token reduction -> COSTO-TOKENS; 4x-4.3x faster end-to-end inference (2.6x-7x speedup even vs vLLM-optimized TextMAS) -> LATENCIA. Implementation Details: m in {0,10,20,40,80} latent-steps swept as a hyperparameter -> evidencia_tipo ABLATION (in addition to BENCHMARK-E2E across 9 benchmarks x 5 backbones, and MEDICION-COSTO via extensive token/speed tables). F differs from F_screening(MULTIAGENTE;COSTO): added WRITE, FIDELIDAD. handoff=CONTENIDO: the substantive reasoning content (latent thoughts + input context) travels agent-to-agent, just encoded as continuous vectors rather than text. plan_estado=NO.

fallos_mitigaciones: Central topic: 'agents either accumulate large volumes of conversational content, including hallucinated or obsolete facts, or depend on opaque, fully LLM-driven memory policies that are costly and difficult to audit' -- retention of hallucinated/outdated information 'can propagate errors into future interactions', while overly conservative admission risks discarding information essential for task continuation. Mitigated by A-MAC's five-signal composite admission score: Confidence C(m) 'directly mitigat[es] hallucination propagation' by requiring ROUGE-L-grounded textual support from prior conversation turns before a candidate is admitted (Eq.2); Novelty N(m) prevents redundant storage via embedding dissimilarity; Recency R(m) exponential decay + Type-Prior T(m) jointly bias against transient/low-value content. Sec.4.3 Ablation Study (Table2) quantifies exactly which factor matters most for reliable admission: removing Type Prior causes the LARGEST F1 drop (0.583->0.476, essentially collapsing to the naive Equal-Weights baseline), while removing Confidence/Recency causes only small drops (-0.015/-0.013) -- an explicit, measured ranking of which safeguard against unreliable memory content is most load-bearing.
cita: Zhang et al. (2026). Adaptive Memory Admission Control for LLM Agents.
notes: Sec.1/3.1: candidate memories are 'semantically atomic piece[s] of information' extracted from multi-turn conversation history for 'multi-session reasoning' -> mem_tipos=SEMANTICA(persistent facts/preferences/identity statements, the Type-Prior feature explicitly distinguishes these from transient content) + EPISODICA(candidates extracted per-turn from dialogue, some event-like). representacion=HIBRIDA: atomic text records + Sentence-BERT embeddings used for the Novelty signal (Eq.3). Eq.1/Algorithm1: S(m)=w1*U+w2*C+w3*N+w4*R+w5*T, admit if S(m)>=theta -> operaciones=ADMISION (the paper's entire contribution, 'memory admission as a structured decision problem' rather than an implicit byproduct); WRITE(candidate extraction+storage); CONSOLIDACION+ACTUALIZACION(Algorithm1 lines5-7: on conflict with an existing memory, 'retain the higher-scoring representation and merge' -- explicit merge-on-conflict). trigger=EVENTO-DETERMINISTA: admission is evaluated deterministically for every extracted candidate (Algorithm1), not LLM-discretionary about WHEN to check, not budget-threshold-based. retrieval=NA/mide_lectura=NO: the paper addresses ONLY the write/admission gate, not how memories are later retrieved for downstream QA (no retrieval mechanism is described or evaluated). alcance=PROYECTO: long-term memory persists 'beyond the context window' across multi-session interaction with the same user. multiagente=NO (single-agent memory-admission architecture; F_screening also omits MULTIAGENTE). fidelidad_procedencia=SI: Confidence C(m) is an explicit grounding/hallucination check (ROUGE-L alignment against supporting conversational spans, Eq.2) before content is trusted enough to enter memory. Table1: A-MAC F1=0.583 vs A-mem(SOTA)=0.541(+7.8%), MemoryBank=0.452(+29.0%), MemGPT=0.324(+80%), with highest precision(0.417) among LLM-based methods at near-perfect recall(0.972) -> metricas EXITO; Table1/4: 31% lower latency than A-mem (2644ms vs 3831ms/candidate), latency breakdown showing the single LLM call (Utility) dominates at 97.6% while 4 rule-based features complete in <65ms combined -> metricas LATENCIA. evidencia_tipo=ABLATION(Table2 explicit per-feature ablation + Table3 threshold sensitivity)+BENCHMARK-E2E(Table1 vs 4 baselines on LoCoMo test N=225)+MEDICION-COSTO(Table4 latency breakdown). F differs from F_screening(WRITE;COSTO): added FIDELIDAD, CONSOLIDACION (no dedicated ADMISION facet exists in the closed F vocabulary). handoff=NO: single-agent, single-user persistent memory across that user's own sessions -- no cross-agent or cross-user content transfer is described. plan_estado=NO: admitted content is user facts/preferences/identity statements, not task-plan/progress state.
